text: What is the strongest argument for keeping state out of components?
choices: Only one component may hold a given piece of state, so a second view is impossible.
The model can then be tested with no screen, in milliseconds, which means those tests actually run in a build.
Components are recreated on every repaint, so state stored in them is lost.
Component state is stored as strings, wasting memory compared to primitive fields.
explanation: Interface tests need a display, are slow, and break when a button moves — so everything you move out of the view becomes testable and everything you leave in effectively is not. That is the same argument Chapter 23 makes about reading the clock: push the decision outward so the logic depends on data rather than on the environment.
